title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium): hold reports for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: The briefing passes: the Government release target and status match the roadmap, and Microsoft documents the quoted report behaviour, permissions and commands. It appropriately distinguishes the cloud-unspecified preview documentation from the planned Government release and leaves its rollout default unstated.

claims.claim: The planned capability is out-of-the-box hold reporting for eDiscovery (Premium) in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview compliance portal:  eDiscovery (Premium) – Hold reports (U.S. Government clouds)

claims.claim: The roadmap describes reports containing information about all legal holds associated with eDiscovery cases.
claims.quote: Out-of-the-box reports that contain information about all legal holds associated with eDiscovery cases in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.

claims.claim: The planned report supports sorting.
claims.quote: Sort and filter your view based on various criteria

claims.claim: The planned report supports filtering.
claims.quote: Sort and filter your view based on various criteria

claims.claim: Aggregated report information can be downloaded for further analysis.
claims.quote: download the aggregated information for further analysis.

claims.claim: The Learn hold report documentation describes a public preview rather than a final Government design.
claims.quote: The hold report is in public preview and provides a tenant-wide summary of hold policies for all eDiscovery cases.

claims.claim: The cited preview hold report page does not identify the clouds it covers.
claims.quote: Searched: "hold report" "GCC" "default"; "hold report" "GCC High" PowerShell portal prerequisites. Read learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-hold-report in full and the GCC, GCC High and DoD deployment pages; the report page names no clouds.

claims.claim: The preview report covers all hold policies in the tenant.
claims.quote: The hold report shows the data locations and reports on all hold policies within the tenant.

claims.claim: The preview report lists locations in both enabled and disabled hold policies.
claims.quote: It lists all locations that are part of those hold policies, whether enabled or disabled.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Policy status column includes Applied partially.
claims.quote: *Applied Partially*: – Indicates that the hold policy that the location is part of is set to be turned on (enabled) and has some locations where the hold might not be applied.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Policy status column includes Policy failed for policies set up incorrectly.
claims.quote: *Policy failed*: Indicates that the policy is set up incorrectly. The policy doesn't have a rule or was set up with rule set as disabled.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Manager (preview) can access the preview hold report.
claims.quote: All eDiscovery Administrators and eDiscovery Managers in your organization can view the Hold Report.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: eDiscovery Managers can view hold reports only for cases they belong to.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Managers can only view hold reports related to the cases they are a member of.

claims.claim: eDiscovery Administrators can see all cases and their hold reports.
claims.quote: Access all cases that are listed on the eDiscovery area in the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Access process and hold reports scoped to all cases.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The cited report page describes viewing and downloading existing hold information, not changing holds through the report.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery hold report read only change holds report switch meter price add-on. Read learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-hold-report in full; its report procedure covers viewing, sorting, filtering, grouping, customising and downloading, not modifying holds.

claims.claim: For Policy failed, Learn instructs readers to create a rule and resync the policy rather than describing a change made by the report.
claims.quote: These policies aren't enforced even if the policy status is successful. To ensure these policies are enforced, create a rule and resync the policy. For more information, see New-CaseHoldRule.

claims.quote: Your organization must have an organization subscription that supports premium eDiscovery features to generate and access the hold report.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate licensing statement specific to the Government hold report is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "hold report" "Government" licensing price subscription. Read the hold report, edisc-get-started, edisc-billing, Purview service description and GCC/GCC High/DoD deployment pages; found premium eDiscovery entitlement but no separate Government hold-report licence.

claims.claim: The hold report page names no meter, price or report-specific add-on.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery hold report meter price add-on (in the read-only/change-holds query); "hold report" "Government" licensing price subscription. Read learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-hold-report, edisc-billing and the Purview service description; no report-specific charge stated.

claims.claim: Managers can be assigned in the Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select eDiscovery Manager. ... Select Edit. ... On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> adds a mail-enabled security group to the Managers subgroup using Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup ... by using the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>

claims.claim: The first Choose users step assigns eDiscovery Managers, not Administrators.
claims.quote: On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups. Search and select the users you want to add as an eDiscovery Manager, then select Select.

claims.claim: The displayed mail-enabled security group assignment is for the Managers subgroup and cannot assign that group to the Administrators subgroup.
claims.quote: You can use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell to add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup ... However, you can't add a mail-enabled security group to the eDiscovery Administrators subgroup.

claims.claim: The preview report is viewed in the Microsoft Purview portal at eDiscovery > Dashboards > Hold report (preview).
claims.quote: The hold report (preview) ... in the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Go to eDiscovery > Dashboards > Hold report (preview) to view your hold report.

claims.claim: Get-CaseHoldPolicy <hold policy name> -Case <case ID> -DistributionDetail is a documented call from the reporting script that reads a policy's distribution details.
claims.quote: $policies = Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Case $cc.Name | % { Get-CaseHoldPolicy $_.Name -Case $_.CaseId -DistributionDetail }

claims.claim: The displayed Get-CaseHoldPolicy call reads hold status rather than enabling or disabling the report.
claims.quote: Get-CaseHoldPolicy $_.Name -Case $_.CaseId -DistributionDetail ... -holdstatus $policy.DistributionStatus -holderror $policy.DistributionResults
